# CityMETER · ศูนย์การค้า (Shopping centers)

> Qualified retail venues of Thailand — shopping centres, community malls, outlets, markets, fuel stations with shops, host stores and retail inside projects — counted under one definition, by district (เขต/อำเภอ), with operators, the shops their lists name, their buildings and the straight-line distance to rail stations (CityMETER Transit). A Landometer CityMETER public research demo, release 0.1.31 (2026-11-08). Research master export 2026-11-07 23:55 ICT, with 12 cells (D41) and 130 cells (D43: 26 venue points moved into the buildings OpenStreetMap names for them) of 01_VENUES written and read back on 2026-11-08; multi-building sites from the site tab read back on 2026-11-08 after three sites were separated from neighbouring venues (D42), One Bangkok's row was filled (D43) and Siam Square's block row was added (D44).

Languages: Thai (the source text) and English (?lang=en, since release 0.7.0, 2026-11-18): the page's words are translated; names are never translated — venues read in the registry's nameEn (about 2,800 are owner-authorised transliterations, not official names), provinces and districts from the boundary files, stations from CityMETER Transit; shop, brand, operator legal names, addresses and records awaiting review stay in Thai as the sources write them. Every figure is the same in both languages. The English is a draft translation.

What one figure means:
- venues (แห่ง) = qualified, countable venues of the research master: several consumer businesses with one common area manager, by source evidence or by a category rule the data owner accepted (the venue panel says which). A parent complex never adds its components. Records still awaiting the definition check, or whose check closed unconfirmed, are grey context dots and never counted. Not a census; not footfall, sales, rent, vacancy, occupancy or market share.
- shops inside (ร้านข้างใน) = branches/listings that 25 registry shop datasets list for a venue, one entry per branch, plus the entries of the centre's own official directory that no brand dataset lists yet (D38, 0.1.27: one name on one floor and unit; brand counters inside department stores, facilities, events and coming-soon rows left out). A venue without a list reads "—", never 0; a shop missing from a list is not shown to be absent; a directory entry is a listed name, not a verified open shop or a legal tenant, and is not in brand search until its brand is linked. A place with sub-areas (a block, a complex) also lists its sub-areas' shops, each naming its sub-area, and counts them once (D41, 0.1.28). Brands with a counter inside a centre's department store are a separate list (แบรนด์ในห้างสรรพสินค้า, D40, 0.1.28), never shops.
- density (แห่ง/ตร.กม.) = venues per km² of the district area of CityMETER production (RTSD 2019 boundaries, production codes).
- distances = straight lines between reference points (haversine), not walking routes or catchments; stations are operating stations only (construction stations are projects, not services).
- size (GLA/GFA) appears only in a venue's own panel; legacy estimates never enter rankings, totals or filters.
- sites = one interior point per building of a multi-building venue (393 venues, 5,746 buildings; a site never holds another venue's building — D42; One Bangkok = its three retail buildings Parade, Post 1928 and The Storeys, while its offices, hotels and residences are background buildings — D43; Siam Square = every building of the block the data owner defined by its roads: 45 site points, drawn as 38 buildings — D44), mostly from OpenStreetMap areas checked with fixed rules (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0); a site is not a land title, a deed area or ownership.
- type groups = the kind of place a user meets (shopping centre, community mall, outlet, market, host store, fuel, retail inside a project); a retail area typed as part of a project but with a name of its own and no qualified parent reads as the place it is (D36, 0.1.23: Chamchuri Square and Park Silom as shopping centres); a counted retail precinct whose sub-areas are shopping centres shows with them (D41, 0.1.28: Siam Square, whose sub-areas Siam Square One, Siam Scape and Centerpoint no longer count on their own); the registry's own type stays in the venue panel.
- 3D buildings = OpenStreetMap first everywhere (building parts, the outline as the podium under them), CityMETER Building V4 only where OpenStreetMap has no building (D35, 0.1.22); heights are OSM tags or CityMETER model estimates, not surveys. A tower over a podium is never drawn as the podium: a piece in the next map tile counts as the same building only with the same height, lying inside it across the tiles' shared strip (D43, 0.1.30).

- next steps in Google (venue panel, D37, 0.1.25) = links to Google AI Mode (a question written for tenants, leasing teams and investors about this exact place), Google Maps (search by name and area) and Street View (a viewpoint on the road in front of the building, facing it). What Google returns — answers, photos, reviews, imagery — is Google's, not CityMETER evidence, and never enters a figure.
- around the centre (รอบศูนย์นี้, release 0.4.0, 2026-11-18) = for the 499 countable shopping centres, community malls and outlets (488 with a point): records that 24 CityMETER research-registry datasets list within straight-line radii of 1, 3 and 5 km of the venue's reference point (not walking distance, not a catchment, not footfall), ranked as mid-rank percentiles among the 488 located venues or the same type; production values (34 CityMETER datasets) of the units the point sits in, ranked per km² within the province or among units that hold venues; rule-based generated priors kept in separate files and never evidence — since 0.5.0 four groups (residents; students and families; workers and commuters; visitors) with a spending-power signal read from observed prices (land appraisal, listing prices and rents, published tuition, recorded starting prices of stays, office asking rents, luxury points of sale; never income or willingness to pay), the observed lines, named records that open in their own CityMETER demo (?e=<kind>:<key>), hypothesis phrases (would pay more for, how they come, formats that fit, what to check) and a 7 × 24 grid relative to the centre's own busiest hour (never footfall). Data: data/locale/ (serving derivative of canonical release venue-locale-shopping-20261120-v0.2.2-rc1 since release 0.9.1, release candidate; signals/NN.json holds the observed context). A dataset without points is never 0; partial datasets carry a star. Since 0.6.0 the section reads visuals first: Aha cards and the comparison chart (measured and benchmark), then the hypotheses drawn without opening (group tiles that open into cards, the 7 × 24 grid, formats that would likely fit under the shop categories of the centre's checked shop list, whose counts are the whole category and never a format; a format the list does not show is a thing to check on site, never absent), then the area, live links and method.
- registered residents around the centre (คนที่มีชื่อในทะเบียนบ้านรอบศูนย์ (แบบจำลอง), release 0.8.0, 2026-11-20) = for the located centres (488; 492 since 0.9.0): people whose names are in the house registration of the buildings whose centre lies within straight-line radii of 1, 3 and 5 km, modelled as production does — each subdistrict's registered population (Department of Provincial Administration, Oct 2026) split over its CityMETER Building V4 buildings by floor area — ranked as mid-rank percentiles among the 488 located centres or the same type; the share of the 5 km figure in the rings 0–1, 1–3 and 3–5 km with people per km², three age groups of the subdistricts covered, and a 250 m grid map whose colours rank the cells within that centre's own 5 km only (the 5 km circles overlap, so cells are never pooled across centres). Not everyone who lives there, not the people who visit the centre, not a catchment, not income or spending power. Data: data/residents/ (release venue-locale-residents-488-20261120-v1).
- comparison of centres and the map as a table (release 0.9.0, 2026-11-20) = every located centre (492) on two ranks — registered residents within the chosen radius (across) and the workers-and-commuters level of the generated prior (up, a rule-based hypothesis, never a count of workers) — in four quarters split at the middle rank (residential, workplace, mixed, sparse: an interpretation), with the five centres of the closest ranks; and a table of people per km² by 8 directions and 3 distances under the residents map. Ranks since 0.9.0 read against a fixed reference: the 488 centres located in release 0.2.0 (meta.reference of data/locale and data/residents); the four centres placed on 2026-11-20 (Market Village Rangsit and Phuket, BALM, Tops Plaza Phichit) are ranked against it and move no published rank. Data: data/compare/residents-workers.json; data/locale/ is the serving derivative of venue-locale-shopping-20261120-v0.2.2-rc1 (release 0.9.1: other centres and markets in the rings read from the 0.9.1 registry, the same 488 reference), data/residents/ of venue-locale-residents-492-20261120-v2.
- every brand in four research datasets (release 0.9.3, 2026-11-20) = car services, hobby stores, pet stores and services, and nail salons count every brand their research master still lists (5,728 · 2,449 · 359 · 132 records; one record per outlet; an in-mall shop without its own point at its shopping centre's point, tied by id), no longer B-Quik, B2S, PETClub or CHABA alone; all four are partial (66 %, 67 %, 30 %, 38 % with a point), so they carry a star and never lead the headline cards.
- places visitors use around the center (release 0.9.4, 2026-11-20) = an inference, not visitors: the located places of 15 stay, retail and service datasets of the locale release (one record = one place, the center itself excluded) within 1 · 3 · 5 km — equal to the release rings — with their rank among the 488 reference centres and a 5 km map per 250 m cell, drawn mint to blue (LDS activity, by the owner's choice, to set it apart from the orange residents map); data/visitors-map/, method DATA_METHOD.md#visitor-places. English mode now shows English basemap names, and the first view fits the highlighted districts to the free map area.
- places people come to work and study around the center (release 0.9.5, 2026-11-20) = an inference, not people or trips: the located places of 7 work, education and health datasets of the locale release (offices, government offices, factories, industrial estates, universities, health facilities, schools; rail stations drawn, not counted) within 1 · 3 · 5 km — equal to the release rings — with their rank among the 488 reference centres and a 5 km map per 250 m cell in cream to navy (LDS count); the students, workers, staff and beds the sources record are shown beside it, never added up; data/work-study-map/, method DATA_METHOD.md#work-study-places.
- office workers (modelled) around the center (release 0.9.6, 2026-11-21) = a model, not a count of employees: office area (the leasable area CityMETER · Office publishes, else the source area) × occupancy (the building's own, else Knight Frank Thailand's Bangkok market rate of Q3 2026, 76.4%) ÷ 10–12 m² per person, as a range per radius, with how many offices have an area; never added to the people the sources record.
- shop logos (release 0.9.7, 2026-11-24) = the logo the CityMETER demo family already verified for a shop's brand, found by the same brand id, the same id in another dataset, or a name the research sheets confirmed (with fixed rewrites such as “Starbucks Coffee” → Starbucks; never a look-alike name); every file checked by SHA-256 against the demo that published it; 8,411 of 26,683 shop entries show a logo (5,182 before). A logo identifies a name on screen: it is not a count, an opening, an official branch or a trademark licence; data/logo-links/, method DATA_METHOD.md#family-logos.
- centre logos (release 0.9.8, 2026-11-24) = a venue the research registry leaves without a logo shows the venue logo another CityMETER demo verified for the same venue id (one artwork, one role; never by name or distance): 157 of 6,266 venues (112 before; +45 from Camera Shops, 34 of them shared chain banners such as Robinson Lifestyle and Lotus's, labelled as such). A logo identifies a venue on screen: it is not a count, an opening or a trademark licence; data/venue-logo-links.json, method DATA_METHOD.md#family-venue-logos.
- research-library shop logos (releases 0.9.9–0.9.11, 2026-11-24) = brands of Optical, Miscellaneous, Hobby, Beauty Clinic and Pharmacy chains show the logo their research master (Pharmacy: its logo library's manifest) recorded, used only when the file's bytes equal the recorded SHA-256, the role is the brand's own mark and the shop lists or the directory links name the brand; 10,489 of 26,683 shop entries show a logo (8,411 before 0.9.9). Same limits as shop logos; data/logo-links/library-receipt.json, method DATA_METHOD.md#library-logos.
- lines on the residents map (release 0.9.2, 2026-11-20) = major roads, rail, rivers (OpenStreetMap via Geofabrik, data to 12 Nov 2026, ODbL) and the operating stations of CityMETER Transit over the 5 km map of every located centre (data/residents-map), with at most 4 road names, 1 river and 3 stations, the nearest first; lines to read the map by, never a network to measure on. The map's legend reads people per 250 × 250 m cell (modelled, two significant figures); every cell is the same area, so the colours are those of people per km².
Snapshot (release 0.9.1, full export of 20 Nov 2026; fixtures, recompute from data):
- 11,142 registry rows; 6,266 qualified; 6,160 countable; 6,154 open or awaiting status, 4 planned, 2 closed; 6,142 located in 733 districts of 77 provinces (Chatuchak Weekend Market added in 0.9.1); 8 of the open or awaiting venues have no point yet (29 placed at owner-identified points in 0.1.27 and 4 in 0.9.0, none field-verified).
- First finding (owner decision D33): 24% of Bangkok's shopping centres, community malls and outlets (58 of 239) are in Pathum Wan, Watthana and Khlong Toei, on 2.2% of its area; 66% of the 58 lie within 500 m of an operating rail station, against 38% (69 of 181) elsewhere in Bangkok. Bangkok holds 679 more places of the other types (D39).
- Shop lists (0.9.1): 26,683 entries at 704 venues = 7,218 brand-dataset listings (checked to 7 Nov) + 19,465 centre-directory entries at 242 centres (export of 18_OFFICIAL_TENANTS of 20 Nov 2026, 31,969 rows at 267 host ids: 19,766 shown, 3,509 already listed, 7,735 shown as 7,268 department-store brands at 18 centres, 959 held). The next line is the 0.1.28 snapshot.
- Shop lists (0.1.28): 22,176 entries at 639 venues = 7,218 brand-dataset listings + 14,958 centre-directory entries at 65 centres (export of 18_OFFICIAL_TENANTS, 26,955 rows: 15,154 shown, 3,161 already listed, 7,735 shown as 7,268 department-store brands at 18 centres, 905 held). Siam Square lists 42 (its own 13 + Siam Square One 27 + Siam Scape 2). The 53 venues of the owner's 7 Nov table: 3,908 listed in 0.1.25, 16,391 now. Brand dataset part: 7,218 displayed listings at 639 hosts from25datasets,1,010 display/search brand-concept keys. All7,108 preceding identities/facts retained;110new listings/16exact-ID corroborations. Six One Bangkok component items are presented once at their retail parent with native child IDs retained. Park Silom23/Central Park64/One Bangkok97. True Digital Park122/17 unchanged. Exact source-to-public coverage audit reads11,139 native inventory rows/26,955 directory observations/211,203 source-link rows;1,129 accepted links still need eligibility review. These populations are not a national physical-tenant census.
- CHAGEE Chamchuri Square and Samyan Mitrtown are distinct branch-host links. Samyan current-open state is owner-reported on 2026-11-07; official locator identity and field operation are separate.
- Native directory research: 26,955 publisher observations at 68 native host IDs / 66 publication groups; source availability queue covers all 11,139 registry rows. Neither a source observation nor an HTTP check is a verified physical outlet.
- Original 31 retail-point audits: 23 selected source-qualified retail/tenant reference points, 8 held without an acceptable point; count roles and venue qualification preserved.
- Every type ranked by count: Mueang Chiang Mai has the most (103, mostly markets).
- Venue points (D43, 0.1.30): 138 counted venues (markets and fuel stations aside) had a reference point outside every drawn building; 26 were moved into the building OpenStreetMap names for them (not field-verified), 112 wait for research. One Bangkok is one place: its point stands in Parade and its 195 directory rows show without zone names.

Deep links (https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/):
- default type set = centres (mall, community, outlet) · ?group=all — every type · ?group={centres|mall|community|outlet|market|hoststore|component|fuel|other}
- ?province={code} — production codes, e.g. BKK, CMI · ?district={code} — e.g. 1007 (เขตปทุมวัน) · ?areas={code},{code} | ?areas=all
- ?venue={venue id} · ?station={CityMETER Transit station id, e.g. RAILCAT:BTS_SUKHUMVIT:CEN} · ?brand={brand key} · ?record={registry id of a context record}
- ?q={text} · ?status={planned|closed|all} · ?operator={group id|__other__|__none__} · ?role={shop role or facility} · ?view={rank|mix|operators} · ?view3d=0 · ?pending=0
- ?lang=en — the same view in English (0.7.0); without it the page is Thai

Data and method:
- [Product statement](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/PRODUCT_STATEMENT.md): users, problem, decisions, red team (§10)
- [Data and method](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/DATA_METHOD.md): definition, counting, first finding, stations, sites, limits
- [Venues](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/venues.json): rows + meta (definitions, counts, checks.firstView)
- [Around the centre](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/locale/meta.json): catalogue of the venue locale bundle; per venue facts in data/locale/facts/NN.json and priors in data/locale/priors/NN.json (NN = FNV-1a of the venue id modulo 64, two digits)
- [Registered residents around the centre](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/residents/meta.json): release and method; per centre data/residents/NNN.json (NNN = FNV-1a of the venue id modulo 128, three digits)
- [Comparison of centres](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/compare/residents-workers.json): every located centre on the two ranks of the comparison chart (0.9.0)
- [Rail stations](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/stations.json) · [Sites](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/venue-sites.json) · [Shop-list index](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/tenant-index.json)

Do not claim from this data: footfall, sales, rent, vacancy, occupancy, market share, a market gap or a "golden location", that a venue is open today, walking time, that being near a station causes visits or sales, that a district without venues has none, that a shop not in a list is absent, or that a building height is measured (CityMETER heights are model estimates).
